# Adjudication Task — Chapter 225

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃225화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|콰직!
  6|
  7|섬뜩한 소리와 함께 흰 이빨들이 허공으로 솟구쳤다.
  8|
  9|얼마나 철저하게 관리했는지 어둠 속에서 반짝반짝 빛이 날 정도다. 이제는 모두 부질없는 일이 되어 버렸지만.
 10|
 11|“프하아아악!”
 12|
 13|쿵!
 14|
 15|수 미터를 날아가 나무에 등을 부딪친 원명훈이 기침을 토해 냈다.
 16|
 17|입안에 남아 있던 이빨들이 피와 섞여 투두둑 떨어졌다. 이내 고개를 든 놈의 얼굴이 경악으로 일그러져 있었다.
 18|
 19|“이, 이게 어떻게…….”
 20|
 21|그야말로 찰나에 벌어진 일.
 22|
 23|비단 원명훈뿐만이 아니라 스타 길드원들 모두가 믿을 수 없다는 표정으로 나를 바라보았다.
 24|
 25|“어떻게는 뭘 어떻게야. 내가 더 강하니까 그런 거지.”
 26|
 27|“이, 이럴 리가 없는데.”
 28|
 29|“응. 있어.”
 30|
 31|산뜻한 대답과 함께 한 걸음을 내딛자 원명훈의 몸이 부르르 떨렸다.
 32|
 33|“오지 마!”
 34|
 35|“내가 왔냐? 너희가 기다리고 있었지.”
 36|
 37|되돌리기에는 이미 늦었다. 이빨을 들이댄 대가를 똑똑히 알려 줄 생각이었다.
 38|
 39|심상치 않은 기색을 느꼈는지 원명훈이 발작처럼 외쳤다.
 40|
 41|“뭐 해, 이 새끼들아!”
 42|
 43|“기, 길드장님.”
 44|
 45|“고작 두 놈이야! 여기서 물러나면 싹 다 죽는 거라고!”
 46|
 47|머뭇거리던 스타 길드원들이 놈의 한마디에 병장기를 치켜세웠다. 원명훈이 얼마 남지 않은 이를 악물었다.
 48|
 49|“이놈은 내가 상대한다. 늙은이부터 잡아!”
 50|
 51|그 말에 발걸음을 멈췄다.
 52|
 53|“지금 뭐라고?”
 54|
 55|“왜, 정곡을 찔렀나?”
 56|
 57|코웃음을 친 원명훈이 이글거리는 눈동자로 나를 노려봤다.
 58|
 59|“진태경, 너 이 새끼. 도대체 무슨 개수작을 부렸는지는 모르지만, 그것도 여기까지다.”
 60|
 61|“개수작?”
 62|
 63|“모르는 척하지 마라. 보나 마나 어디서 성능 좋은 가속 장비를 구해서 걸쳤나 본데…….”
 64|
 65|“아, 그 얘기였어?”
 66|
 67|나는 놀라움에 눈을 크게 떴다.
 68|
 69|어떻게든 자신이 진 이유를 합리화시키는 원명훈의 상상력이 놀라울 지경이다.
 70|
 71|“그거 상당히 참신한 생각인데. 그런데 그에 비해서 인질극은 너무 상투적이지 않나?”
 72|
 73|“상투적이지만 늘 먹힌다는 게 중요하지.”
 74|
 75|“글쎄…….”
 76|
 77|나는 말꼬리를 흐렸다.
 78|
 79|원명훈과 몇 마디를 주고받는 사이 탱커를 앞세운 스타 길드원들이 김 집사를 향해 돌격하고 있었다.
 80|
 81|“이번에는 좀. 경우가 다를 것 같은데.”
 82|
 83|“뭐?”
 84|
 85|원명훈이 반문한 그 순간, 허리를 두드리고 있던 김 집사가 길쭉한 지팡이를 땅에 찍었다.
 86|
 87|가벼운 동작. 그러나 지팡이 끝에서 흘러나온 힘은 지면을 뒤흔들었다.
 88|
 89|이어진 중후한 목소리는 폭탄의 마지막 스위치나 다름없었다.
 90|
 91|“뒤엎어라. 어스퀘이크(Earthquake).”
 92|
 93|구구궁!
 94|
 95|자연을 간직한 원시림이 크게 몸을 떨었다.
 96|
 97|단단한 지면에 금이 가자 흙과 바위가 튀어 올랐고, 깊이 뿌리 내린 나무의 줄기가 모습을 드러냈다. 이름을 알 수 없는 날짐승들이 무리 지어 날아올랐다.
 98|
 99|- 삐이이익!
100|
101|지진을 피할 수 있었던 것은 거기까지였다.
102|
103|불행하게도 스타 길드원들에게는 날개가 없었고, 갈라지고 박살 난 지면은 삼각파도가 되어 그들을 집어삼켰다.
104|
105|“모두 피해…… 크억!”
106|
107|“으아아아악!”
108|
109|콰아아아아!
110|
111|파도가 휩쓸고 지나간 자리에는 신음과 비명만이 드문드문 흘렀다.
112|
113|스타 길드원들은 엄청난 무게의 토사(土砂)에 짓눌려 간신히 목만 내놓은 채 숨을 몰아쉬었다.
114|
115|단 한 번의 마법으로 B급 베테랑 헌터 십여 명을 전투 불능 상태로 만든 이는 태연하기 그지없었다.
116|
117|“젊은 친구들이 선배에 대한 예의가 없군. 다들 힘 빼고 눈 감게. 이대로 파묻혀 죽기 싫으면.”
118|
119|이제껏 들어 본 적 없는 서늘한 목소리다.
120|
121|비로소 김 집사의 진짜 실력을 알아차린 스타 길드원들이 창백하게 질린 얼굴로 고개를 떨궜다.
122|
123|아, 한 사람은 제외하고.
124|
125|“A급 마법사……!”
126|
127|A급 헌터는 드물지만, 그중에서도 마법, 힐러 계열은 더더욱 희귀하다. 항상 뒷짐만 지고 허허 웃던 김 집사가 A급 마법사라고는 아마 예상하지 못했을 것이다.
128|
129|나는 몸을 부들부들 떠는 원명훈을 보며 씩 웃었다.
130|
131|“인질극 실패했다. 이제 어쩌냐?”
132|
133|“…….”
134|
135|“그래서 말했잖아. 이빨 들이대지 말라고.”
136|
137|넋 나간 사람처럼 멍하니 서 있던 원명훈이 가까스로 입을 열었다.
138|
139|“너는, 너희는 뭐지?”
140|
141|“알고 있잖아, 평화 길드. 길드 이름값 하고 싶은데 주위에서 협조를 안 해 줘서 문제지.”
142|
143|원명훈이 입술을 깨물었다.
144|
145|한순간의 잘못된 선택이 지금 같은 결과를 불러올 것이라고는 감히 상상조차 할 수 없었겠지.
146|
147|하지만 이미 되돌리기에는 늦었다. 궁지에 몰린 하이에나에게 남은 방법은 두 가지뿐이다.
148|
149|‘도망치거나. 굴복하거나.’
150|
151|원명훈은 후자를 택했다.
152|
153|터텅!
154|
155|그의 손아귀에서 미끄러진 창이 땅을 뒹굴었다.
156|
157|“……항복하겠다.”
158|
159|“항복?”
160|
161|나는 원명훈을 향해 다가갔다. 땅에 떨어진 창을 멀리 걷어차자 그가 체념한 듯 고개를 숙였다.
162|
163|“이렇게 갑자기?”
164|
165|“…….”
166|
167|코앞에 있음에도 아무런 움직임이 없다. 고개를 숙인 채 대답하지 않는 그를 향해 물었다.
168|
169|“나가면 넌 최소 무기징역이야. 게이트에서 지금 같은 행위가 얼마나 중범죄인지 모르지 않을 텐데?”
170|
171|머뭇거리던 원명훈이 입을 열었다.
172|
173|“죽는 것보다는 나으니까.”
174|
175|“죽는 것보다는 낫다…… 그래, 그건 맞는 말이지.”
176|
177|살아남는다면 기회는 있다. 그러나 죽음은 완전한 종결을 의미한다. 그 너머에 무엇이 있는지는 그 후에 알게 될 일이다.
178|
179|잃을 것이 많은 자는 죽음이 두려운 법. 지금의 원명훈이 바로 그랬다.
180|
181|“고개 들어.”
182|
183|“……알았다.”
184|
185|나는 그의 눈을 물끄러미 들여다보았다. 무저갱처럼 컴컴한 한 쌍의 눈동자에는 알 수 없는 빛이 소용돌이치고 있었다.
186|
187|앞으로 펼쳐질 미래에 대한 두려움. 죽음에 대한 불안감.
188|
189|그리고…….
190|
191|털썩!
192|
193|“태경아. 제발.”
194|
195|“…….”
196|
197|“한 번만, 마지막으로 한 번만 기회를 주라. 나 같은 놈 죽여 봤자 찝찝함만 남을 뿐이야.”
198|
199|“찝찝하지만 처벌은 받지 않겠지. 게이트에서 살해 위협을 당했을 시 정당방위가 인정된다. 당신도 잘 알잖아.”
200|
201|“그, 그래도.”
202|
203|원명훈이 침을 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
204|
205|“날 죽이면 살인이야. 네가 살인자가 된다는 사실은 변하지 않는다고.”
206|
207|살인자. 혀끝에서 굴러가는 그 단어가 텁텁하다.
208|
209|무릎을 꿇은 채 비굴한 목소리로 목숨을 구걸하는 원명훈의 모습을 바라보다가 입을 열었다.
210|
211|“믿어 주지.”
212|
213|“태경아!”
214|
215|“부탁인데, 내 믿음을 배신하지 마.”
216|
217|스스로 포박하라는 말과 함께 밧줄을 던져 주고 돌아선 그 순간이었다.
218|
219|“으하하! 이 멍청한 새끼!”
220|
221|환희에 찬 외침과 동시에 등 뒤에서 느껴지는 살기.
222|
223|고개를 돌리자 코앞까지 들이닥친 원명훈이 보였다. 그의 손에는 어느새 오러가 서린 단검이 들려 있었다.
224|
225|“뒈져!”
226|
227|쉬쉭! 촤아아악!
228|
229|짧은 파공성과 함께 솟구치는 피 분수. 기쁨으로 환하게 밝혀져 있던 원명훈의 얼굴에 의아함이 깃들었다.
230|
231|“……어?”
232|
233|투둑.
234|
235|한 박자 늦게 뭔가가 땅에 떨어진다.
236|
237|깔끔하게 잘려 나간 단면, 오러가 사라진 단검을 꽉 움켜쥐고 있는 그것은 원명훈의 손목이었다.
238|
239|“그보다 두 배는 더 빨랐어야지.”
240|
241|손에 든 비수에서 피를 털어 냈다. 찰나의 순간, 나는 인벤토리에서 무기를 꺼내 들었고 승부는 순식간에 갈렸다.
242|
243|짧지만 억겁과도 같은 침묵.
244|
245|이내 원명훈의 입이 서서히 벌어지더니 끔찍한 비명이 터져 나왔다.
246|
247|“크아아아아악!”
248|
249|고통에 몸부림치는 놈을 바라보는 내 마음은 호수처럼 잔잔하고 평온하기만 했다.
250|
251|믿어서는 안 될 놈을 믿었다는 배신감도, 일말의 후회도 들지 않았다.
252|
253|왜냐하면…….
254|
255|“고맙다. 믿었던 그대로 움직여 줘서.”
256|
257|나는 애초부터 원명훈을 믿지 않았으니까.
258|
259|예티의 목걸이를 받았을 때부터, 놈이 내 경고를 무시하고 다시 이빨을 드러낸 그 순간부터.
260|
261|“넌 딱 그 정도 인간이었어.”
262|
263|“끄윽, 끄아아악!”
264|
265|“살려 둔다면 언제고 다시 이빨을 들이대겠지. 목에 걸린 가시처럼, 살아난다면 어떻게든 다시 돌아올 거야.”
266|
267|서걱, 서걱!
268|
269|비수가 종아리의 힘줄을 갈랐다. 피가 튀고 무릎이 꺾인다. 시퍼렇게 날이 선 비수를 놈의 목에 붙인 그때였다.
270|
271|“진태경 헌터님!”
272|
273|수십 미터 밖, 김 집사가 만류 어린 눈빛으로 바라보고 있었다.
274|
275|“그렇게까지 하실 필요는 없습니다.”
276|
277|“맞아요. 그래서 한 번 놔준 거고.”
278|
279|“하지만 몬스터를 죽이는 것과 살인은 다릅니다. 차라리 제가.”
280|
281|나는 침착한 목소리로 대꾸했다.
282|
283|“압니다.”
284|
285|“……네?”
286|
287|“이미 잘 알고 있어요.”
288|
289|지금까지 몇 명을 죽였을까. 수십? 아니면 일백?
290|
291|내가 살아온 세상은 호락호락하지 않았다. 게이트에서는 몬스터를 죽여야 했고, 무림에서는 사람을 죽여야 했다.
292|
293|나는 고고한 성인군자가 아니다. 가족이 있고 지켜야 할 사람이 있는 헌터이자 무인이다. 살아남기 위해서, 강해지기 위해서라면 기꺼이 피를 묻힐 수 있다.
294|
295|그런 내게 있어 몬스터와 눈앞의 원명훈은 큰 차이가 없다.
296|
297|‘적이니까.’
298|
299|그 상대가 누구건, 언젠가 나와 내 사람들에게 위해를 끼칠 만한 적이라면 화근을 없애 버려야 옳다.
300|
301|“그러니 말리지 마세요.”
302|
303|“……!”
304|
305|김 집사도 숱한 전장을 헤쳐 온 사람이다.
306|
307|짧은 대화만으로도 알아차렸을 것이다. 내가 어떤 사람이며 무슨 결심을 했는지를.
308|
309|가라앉은 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 그가 살짝 고개를 끄덕였다.
310|
311|“끄으으으. 사, 살려…….”
312|
313|“살려 달라고?”
314|
315|신음을 흘리는 원명훈을 내려다봤다.
316|
317|어린 시절 우러러보던 우상. 수많은 별 중에서도 유달리 빛나던 그였다.
318|
319|하지만 그에 대한 옛 기억은 이제 타임캡슐에 넣어 깊숙이 묻어 둘 것이다.
320|
321|나는 작은 목소리로 속삭였다.
322|
323|“누군가를 죽이려고 했으면, 죽을 각오도 했어야지.”
324|
325|“태, 태경아. 제발…….”
326|
327|서걱!
328|

Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. # Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 225

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃225화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|콰직!
  6|
  7|섬뜩한 소리와 함께 흰 이빨들이 허공으로 솟구쳤다.
  8|
  9|얼마나 철저하게 관리했는지 어둠 속에서 반짝반짝 빛이 날 정도다. 이제는 모두 부질없는 일이 되어 버렸지만.
 10|
 11|“프하아아악!”
 12|
 13|쿵!
 14|
 15|수 미터를 날아가 나무에 등을 부딪친 원명훈이 기침을 토해 냈다.
 16|
 17|입안에 남아 있던 이빨들이 피와 섞여 투두둑 떨어졌다. 이내 고개를 든 놈의 얼굴이 경악으로 일그러져 있었다.
 18|
 19|“이, 이게 어떻게…….”
 20|
 21|그야말로 찰나에 벌어진 일.
 22|
 23|비단 원명훈뿐만이 아니라 스타 길드원들 모두가 믿을 수 없다는 표정으로 나를 바라보았다.
 24|
 25|“어떻게는 뭘 어떻게야. 내가 더 강하니까 그런 거지.”
 26|
 27|“이, 이럴 리가 없는데.”
 28|
 29|“응. 있어.”
 30|
 31|산뜻한 대답과 함께 한 걸음을 내딛자 원명훈의 몸이 부르르 떨렸다.
 32|
 33|“오지 마!”
 34|
 35|“내가 왔냐? 너희가 기다리고 있었지.”
 36|
 37|되돌리기에는 이미 늦었다. 이빨을 들이댄 대가를 똑똑히 알려 줄 생각이었다.
 38|
 39|심상치 않은 기색을 느꼈는지 원명훈이 발작처럼 외쳤다.
 40|
 41|“뭐 해, 이 새끼들아!”
 42|
 43|“기, 길드장님.”
 44|
 45|“고작 두 놈이야! 여기서 물러나면 싹 다 죽는 거라고!”
 46|
 47|머뭇거리던 스타 길드원들이 놈의 한마디에 병장기를 치켜세웠다. 원명훈이 얼마 남지 않은 이를 악물었다.
 48|
 49|“이놈은 내가 상대한다. 늙은이부터 잡아!”
 50|
 51|그 말에 발걸음을 멈췄다.
 52|
 53|“지금 뭐라고?”
 54|
 55|“왜, 정곡을 찔렀나?”
 56|
 57|코웃음을 친 원명훈이 이글거리는 눈동자로 나를 노려봤다.
 58|
 59|“진태경, 너 이 새끼. 도대체 무슨 개수작을 부렸는지는 모르지만, 그것도 여기까지다.”
 60|
 61|“개수작?”
 62|
 63|“모르는 척하지 마라. 보나 마나 어디서 성능 좋은 가속 장비를 구해서 걸쳤나 본데…….”
 64|
 65|“아, 그 얘기였어?”
 66|
 67|나는 놀라움에 눈을 크게 떴다.
 68|
 69|어떻게든 자신이 진 이유를 합리화시키는 원명훈의 상상력이 놀라울 지경이다.
 70|
 71|“그거 상당히 참신한 생각인데. 그런데 그에 비해서 인질극은 너무 상투적이지 않나?”
 72|
 73|“상투적이지만 늘 먹힌다는 게 중요하지.”
 74|
 75|“글쎄…….”
 76|
 77|나는 말꼬리를 흐렸다.
 78|
 79|원명훈과 몇 마디를 주고받는 사이 탱커를 앞세운 스타 길드원들이 김 집사를 향해 돌격하고 있었다.
 80|
 81|“이번에는 좀. 경우가 다를 것 같은데.”
 82|
 83|“뭐?”
 84|
 85|원명훈이 반문한 그 순간, 허리를 두드리고 있던 김 집사가 길쭉한 지팡이를 땅에 찍었다.
 86|
 87|가벼운 동작. 그러나 지팡이 끝에서 흘러나온 힘은 지면을 뒤흔들었다.
 88|

[P86]
“It’s better than dying.”

[P87]
“Better than dying… Yeah, that’s true.”

[P88]
As long as he survived, there would still be a chance. Death, on the other hand, meant a complete end. Whatever lay beyond it was something he would only discover afterward.

[P89]
People with a lot to lose tended to fear death. Won Myunghoon was no exception.

[P90]
“Raise your head.”

[P91]
“……All right.”

[P92]
I stared into his eyes.

[P93]
An unknowable light swirled within those twin pupils, dark as the abyss.

[P94]
Fear of the future awaiting him. Anxiety over death.

[P95]
And…

[P96]
Thump!

[P97]
“Taekyung. Please.”

[P98]
“……”

[P99]
“Just once. Give me one last chance. Killing someone like me will only leave a bad taste in your mouth.”

[P100]
“It might leave a bad taste, but I won’t be punished for it. Self-defense applies when someone threatens to kill you inside a Gate. You know that as well as I do.”

[P101]
“B-But still.”

[P102]
Won Myunghoon swallowed hard.

[P103]
“If you kill me, it’s murder. That doesn’t change the fact that you’ll become a murderer.”

[P104]
*Murderer.*

[P105]
The word tasted bitter on my tongue.

[P106]
I looked down at Won Myunghoon, kneeling before me and begging for his life in a servile voice, then spoke.

[P107]
“I’ll trust you.”

[P108]
“Taekyung!”

[P109]
“But do me a favor. Don’t betray that trust.”

[P110]
I tossed him a rope and told him to bind himself. The moment I turned away—

[P111]
“Ha-ha-ha! You stupid bastard!”

[P112]
A triumphant shout rang out, and killing intent flared behind me.

[P113]
I turned my head. Won Myunghoon was already right on top of me, an Aura-infused dagger clutched in his hand.

[P114]
“Die!”

[P115]
Whoosh! Slash!

[P116]
A brief rush of displaced air—and a fountain of blood sprayed upward. The triumphant joy lighting Won Myunghoon’s face gave way to bewilderment.

[P117]
“……Huh?”

[P118]
Thud.

[P119]
A moment later, something fell to the ground.

[P120]
It was Won Myunghoon’s wrist, cleanly severed and still clutching the dagger whose Aura had vanished.

[P121]
“You needed to be at least twice that fast.”

[P122]
I flicked the blood from the dagger in my hand. In that split second, I had drawn a weapon from my Inventory, and the fight had ended just as quickly.

[P123]
A brief silence followed, though it felt like an eternity.

[P124]
Then Won Myunghoon’s mouth slowly fell open, and a horrific scream burst from it.

[P125]
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaah!”

[P126]
As I watched him writhe in agony, my heart remained as still and peaceful as a lake.

[P127]
I felt no betrayal at having trusted someone I should never have trusted. Not even the slightest regret.

[P128]
Because…

[P129]
“Thanks. You did exactly what I trusted you to do.”

[P130]
I had never trusted Won Myunghoon in the first place.

[P131]
Not since I received Yeti’s Necklace. Not since the moment he ignored my warning and bared his teeth at me again.

[P132]
“You were always exactly this kind of man.”

[P133]
“Urgh, gyaaaaah!”

[P134]
“If I leave you alive, you’ll bare your teeth at me again someday. Like a thorn stuck in my throat, you’ll find some way to come back as long as you survive.”

[P135]
Slice. Slice.

[P136]
My dagger severed the tendons in his calf. Blood spattered, and his knee buckled. Just as I pressed the razor-sharp blade against his throat—

[P137]
“Hunter Jin Taekyung!”

[P138]
Several dozen meters away, Butler Kim was watching me with concern in his eyes.

[P139]
“There is no need to go that far.”

[P140]
“You’re right. That’s why I let him go once.”

[P141]
“But killing a monster and murdering a person are different. I would rather do it myself—”

[P142]
I answered calmly.

[P143]
“I know.”

[P144]
“……Pardon?”

[P145]
“I know that perfectly well.”

[P146]
How many people had I killed by now? Dozens? Maybe a hundred?

[P147]
The worlds I had lived in had never been forgiving. Inside Gates, I had to kill monsters. In Murim, I had to kill people.

[P148]
I was no lofty junzi. I was a Hunter and a martial artist with a family and people I had to protect. If surviving and becoming stronger meant getting blood on my hands, I would do it willingly.

[P149]
To me, there was little difference between a monster and Won Myunghoon.

[P150]
*He was an enemy.*

[P151]
Whoever the enemy might be, if they could someday bring harm to me or my people, the right thing to do was eliminate the threat at its source.

[P152]
“So don’t stop me.”

[P153]
“……!”

[P154]
Butler Kim had fought his way through countless battlefields himself.

[P155]
That brief exchange must have been enough for him to understand what kind of person I was—and what I had decided to do.

[P156]
He regarded me with a grave look, then gave a small nod.

[P157]
“Urgh. P-Please…spare me…”

[P158]
“Spare you?”

[P159]
I looked down at the groaning Won Myunghoon.

[P160]
He had once been the idol I looked up to as a child, a man who had shone brighter than any of the countless stars around him.

[P161]
But now I would seal those old memories inside a time capsule and bury them deep underground.

[P162]
I whispered quietly.

[P163]
“If you were going to kill someone, you should’ve been prepared to die.”

[P164]
“Ta-Taekyung. Please…”

[P165]
Slice!

[P166]
The dagger cut deep into his throat. Won Myunghoon’s eyes bulged as he stared up at me pleadingly.

[P167]
He tried to cover the wound with his one remaining hand, but he could stop neither the blood nor his life from pouring out.

[P168]
Grrrgh. Thud.

[P169]
The moment his body collapsed with a wet, rattling gurgle—

[P170]
> **System**
>
> - You have defeated **Lv. 80 Won Myunghoon**!
>
> - You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP!

[P171]
The System announced the enemy’s death.

[P172]
“Let’s go.”

[P173]
Butler Kim nodded, regarding me with an unreadable look.

[P174]
“We have more baggage to take with us now.”

[P175]
He waved his staff, and the Star Guild members buried beneath the earth floated gently into the air.

[P176]
As I watched conjured ropes bind them tightly together like strings of dried fish, something occurred to me.

[P177]
“Wait a moment, Butler Kim.”

[P178]
“……?”

[P179]
“We need to add one more person.”

[P180]
A short while later, I followed my Qi Sense and found a gagged man.

[P181]
For some reason, he had been bound tightly to a tree. And I recognized his face.

[P182]
“The Star Guild’s Team One Leader?”

[P183]
* * *

[P184]
Most of the reporters who had flocked there to cover the joint raid between the Peace Guild and the Star Guild—or rather, the raid led by Jin Taekyung and Won Myunghoon—had left long ago.

[P185]
But there were always exceptions. One was a young man in thick, horn-rimmed glasses, eating ramen.

[P186]
“Being the youngest is miserable. Just miserable.”

[P187]
His colleague snickered and picked up a piece of instant kimchi.

[P188]
“You’ve only been here two months, and you’re already full of complaints.”

[P189]
“Come on, Senior. You haven’t been here that long either.”

[P190]
“Hey. Back in my day, I kept my mouth shut and did what I was told. If they told me to stay, I stayed. If they told me to tear someone apart in print, I did it.”

[P191]
“But isn’t this a bit much? How can they make us wait around for days just to cover one Hunter?”

[P192]
“You haven’t changed since college. If you don’t like it, stick around long enough to build up some seniority.”

[P193]
The young man stared glumly into his cup ramen, where beads of oil floated across the surface.

[P194]
“It’s an A-Rank Gate. It’ll take at least three days for them to come out…”

[P195]
“Three days? We should count ourselves lucky if they don’t stay the whole week.”

[P196]
“A week?”

[P197]
“It’s an A-Rank Gate. Once they’re inside, they might as well get everything they can out of it.”

[P198]
“……Ugh.”

[P199]
The young man shuddered as if the mere thought gave him goose bumps.

[P200]
Seeing groups of other junior reporters in the same miserable situation eating nearby only made him feel worse.

[P201]
“I wish they’d come out soon.”

[P202]
“They definitely won’t be out today. Like you said, even if they’re quick, it’ll still take three days. Get some sleep. Want to hit a sauna together? Maybe play some billiards?”

[P203]
“Billiards?”

[P204]
“Yeah. There’s plenty to do around here. The local businesses just rip you off.”

[P205]
“Then maybe one game…”

[P206]
Tempted by his Senior’s offer, the young reporter had just begun to rise when—

[P207]
Whoooooosh.

[P208]
The enormous door looming before them—the Gate—gave off a strange sound.

[P209]
The mana that had lain as still as the surface of a lake began to swirl, and urgent shouts erupted from every direction.

[P210]
“The Gate! The Gate is opening!”

[P211]
“Already? What the hell?”

[P212]
“The cameras! Get them over here, now!”

[P213]
The area descended into chaos. The reporters who had been idly passing the time shot to their feet and crowded in front of the Gate.

[P214]
The young reporter and his Senior were no exception. They secured a place at the front faster than anyone else and frantically began preparing.

[P215]
“What’s going on? Why are they coming out already?”

[P216]
“How should I know? Set up the equipment!”

[P217]
Cameras began rolling, and flashes burst without pause.

[P218]
The reporters sensed that something had happened, and their instincts proved exactly right.

[P219]
Whoosh!

[P220]
Around a dozen people burst from the swirling vortex of mana.

[P221]
Everyone who saw them stared with their mouths hanging open.

[P222]
“……W-What happened?”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
